claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA contains a ductile FCC matrix and a B2 phase and exhibits high elongation.
The as-cast alloy has no significant L12 ordering or jagged phase boundaries.
Aging at 600°C produces peak L12 ordering with local chemistry approaching Ni3Al stoichiometry.
Aging at 600°C forms jagged B2/FCC interfaces.
Increasing L12 order toward a critical threshold increases or maximizes the antiphase boundary energy.
The highly ordered 600°C state has reduced stacking-fault energy.
The combination of high antiphase boundary energy and reduced stacking-fault energy inhibits dislocation cross-slip and forces planar slip.
Jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries act as mechanical stress concentrators.
Planar slip terminating at jagged phase boundaries generates severe local stress concentrations that cause brittle fracture at 600°C aging.
Aging at 750°C reduces the L12 order parameter and lowers the antiphase boundary energy.
Reduced ordering after 750°C aging restores cross-slip and ductility.
Ductility varies non-monotonically with aging temperature and has a sharp minimum near 600°C.
The 600°C-aged state will have a significantly higher nanoindentation pop-in load than the 750°C-aged state.
The 600°C-aged state will have a smaller nanoindentation pop-in displacement than the 750°C-aged state.
TEM will reveal a high density of planar slip bands terminating at jagged phase boundaries in the 600°C-aged brittle state.
Planar slip bands terminating at jagged phase boundaries will be absent in the ductile 750°C-aged state.
The brittle transition requires the L12 order parameter to exceed a critical value and also requires jagged phase boundaries.
Smoothing the phase boundaries may suppress the brittle transition even after aging at 600°C with high L12 order.
An 800°C post-aging anneal for one hour can reduce L12 order without significantly changing phase-boundary morphology.
High local deformation stress may destroy short-range order and thereby complicate observation of the proposed mechanism.
